Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- 7 days of fever with alternating hot/cold episodes, night sweats, diffuse myalgias, nausea, fatigue; minimal oral intake. No localizing respiratory, ENT, GI, urinary, or CNS symptoms. Recent multi-week travel across Vietnam including rural/farmland exposure; returned 4 weeks ago. Took daily malaria prophylaxis (drug unknown). Occupational exposure as nurse. Allergies: pollen (hay fever)
- Assessment: Undifferentiated febrile illness post–SE Asia travel; malaria and other travel-related infections must be excluded. No exam or vitals obtained via teleconsultation
- Plan from transcript: Urgent in-person clinical examination today at central London clinic (or local A&E if more convenient). Post-exam blood tests to include malaria thick and thin films and inflammatory markers, with additional tests at clinician’s discretion. Patient advised not to work until evaluated. Admin to arrange booking; patient to call provided number and present consultation note
- DDx alignment:
  - Malaria (High likelihood): Travel to Vietnam with rural exposure; paroxysmal fevers/chills/sweats, myalgias, nausea; prophylaxis is not fully protective. Thick/thin films requested
  - Enteric fever (Moderate likelihood): Prolonged fever with minimal localization post–SE Asia travel; exposure across varied settings. No abdominal symptoms recorded
  - Common viral syndrome (Moderate likelihood): Systemic symptoms could reflect viral illness; healthcare worker exposure. Lack of URI symptoms noted
- No contradictions between transcript and DDx noted

Management Plan
- Immediate: Attend central London clinic today for examination; alternative is local A&E if needed
- Testing: Malaria thick and thin films; inflammatory markers; additional general blood tests per examining clinician after assessment
- Work: Do not attend work until evaluation completed
- Administration: Clinician to message admin for same-day booking; patient to call provided number and show these notes

Consider:
- Pathology tests as above: Considered and planned (malaria films, inflammatory markers; others per exam)
- EPC referral for allied health (10x visits/year): Not recorded

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Malaria (High): Compatible travel, timing, paroxysmal fevers/chills/sweats, myalgias; prophylaxis not fully protective; specific testing planned
- Enteric fever (Moderate): SE Asia travel with variable exposures; persistent fever with minimal localization; GI features not reported
- Common viral syndrome (Moderate): Systemic symptoms and occupational exposure; absence of focal bacterial source
